evidence.note: Reviewed the full new test-log Builder: stamping, chain derivation via LineHash of the previous canonical line, Init/Event defaults, and Copy fork semantics (Origin, lineage, fresh Seq/Prev).

Reviewed 928 lines of store conformance tests: create/append CAS, lock contention, MaxEvents, torn-tail repair and sidecars, symlink and permission path refusals, List ordering and error rows, external oracle fixture.

Reviewed canonical-form, hash, CapText boundary and value-pin tests; assertions match the documented contract (whitespace stripping, key order, duplicate-key rejection, idempotence, UTF-8 safe truncation).
Reviewed decision-mapping table cases and the nil-judge executor test asserting CodeExecutorFailed with reason no_judge.
Reviewed the new 0.9.0 and 0.8.3 sections; documentation only, consistent with the FSM feature set described elsewhere in the branch.
Reviewed the new per-package coverage floor list; data file with a regeneration comment, no internal/fsm entries (those are gated at 100% separately).

Ran go vet over internal/fsm/run and internal/fsm/kind: clean. Confirmed every Override constructor in builder.go has at least one call site elsewhere in the tree, so no dead exported API. No TODO/FIXME markers, no eval-style execution, and every chunk in this shard is part 1/1 (no truncated diff context).

findings.note: Builder.stamp declares a third parameter as the blank identifier (_ []Override) and never applies it; Init passes its overrides to stamp anyway and then applies them itself in the loop that follows. The dead parameter reads as if stamp honours overrides and invites a future caller to rely on that. Drop the parameter or apply it inside stamp.

evidence.note: func (b *Builder) stamp(typ string, data any, _ []Override) Event — third argument ignored
Init calls b.stamp(TypeInit, d, o) then re-applies o in its own loop

findings.note: The torn-tail sidecar permission assertion stats matches[0] (the lexicographically first sidecar accumulated across loop iterations) rather than the sidecar this iteration created, and discards the Stat error, so a nil FileInfo would panic instead of failing the test cleanly. Assert on the sidecar whose bytes were just matched.

evidence.note: fi, _ := os.Stat(matches[0]) followed by fi.Mode().Perm() != 0o600 inside the per-tail loop

findings.note: The mk helper in TestSummarizeIncompleteFork declares kind Kind and extra ...string parameters that are never used (kind is explicitly discarded with _ = kind, extra is never referenced) and has a single call site passing an empty kind. Dead test scaffolding; simplify the signature to mk(to int64).

evidence.note: mk := func(to int64, kind Kind, extra ...string) Log { ... _ = kind ... }
_ = kind discard proving the parameter is unused
